scientific_question: Do positive mule-deer versus negative bighorn q~astronomical daylength source associations persist in the SAME published Wyoming original GPS study after requiring BOTH native taxa observed on the SAME calendar-year / local-astronomical dates across ORIGINAL UTC-hourbin, EVEN 2h and ODD 2h acquisition schedules?
source_integrity: Verify original Movebank exact source bitstream UUID/file bytes/provider MD5, then replay BOTH original native q/night-day and q~daylength all-source means/tag numbers, and both native complete three-schedule q/daylight group effects to 1e-12 BEFORE shared-date filtering. One original DOI, not two independent ecosystems.
prior_outcome_disclosure: This was chosen AFTER observing opposite nominal daylength slopes in the original strict triple subset; the new study is an exploratory support-quality falsification attempt, not a preregistered or untouched independent replication.

date_filter.initial_triple_source: For each original tagged individual and calendar year, intersect local astronomical dates with at least 3 DAY and 3 NIGHT source-valid straight-line GPS intervals in ALL original, EVEN and ODD schedules.
date_filter.exact_study_date: A local astronomical date belongs to the same-study comparison only if at least one originally eligible tagged individual in EACH of the two taxa has triple-qualified source GPS data on exactly that YEAR+DATE.
date_filter.iterative_support: From original tag-year entries with >=10 triple date records and daylength spread>=0.5h, repeatedly intersect dates supported by both taxa and remove tag-year entries that lack >=10 study-shared dates or daylight range 0.5h until fixed point. Never choose dates based on q or slope magnitude/sign.
date_filter.standard_photoperiod_x: Compute a common astronomical daylight-hours axis at a fixed reference latitude of 43.0°N, declared before processing data, for every shared solar calendar date in the Wyoming study; 43N is a standardized study-region reference rather than the actual per-animal daylength or received sunshine.
date_filter.unchanged_schedule_intervals: ORIGINAL q uses accepted actual 0.5-2.0h original GPS intervals, EVEN and ODD use accepted actual 1.5-2.5h original original-fix subsets; <=60km/h and same solar day/part at segment start/midpoint/end. No interpolation.
date_filter.original_tag_unit: For each retained tagged animal, calculate three within-year q~common-L slopes, then equal-weight original eligible years per tag. Require >=5 distinct original tags/taxon to publish group estimate.
date_filter.minimum_date_level: For pooled calendar-date study comparison, >=20 shared dates, reference daylength range>=0.5h, and >=5 independent year-month blocks with at least two distinct daylength values; otherwise date-level slope contrast stays UNAVAILABLE.
date_filter.no_source_selection: All two native taxa must remain; if no shared season support, preserve INSUFFICIENT_COMMON_DATE_SUPPORT rather than adding new source/year/day or relabeling original exploratory result.

outcomes.primary: Within-one-original-study mule deer and bighorn q~common reference astronomical daylength slope, each source tag mean (per schedule); and mule minus bighorn slope difference with independently resampled original tagged animals 2000 times; source group/bootstrap95 nominal and signs, not world confidence.
outcomes.secondary: On exactly same source calendar-year/local astronomical dates, compute daily species q means (each taxon equal 1 regardless of GPS tags) then slope of (mule q minus bighorn q) vs shared standardized 43N daylength, with 2000 year-month block bootstrap draws; exploratory paired calendar-date analysis, not original-tag experimental treatment.
outcomes.source_frame: One original Wyoming study with two native taxa; both species sampled in same published source but may occupy different microhabitats, collar duty cycles or climate histories.
outcomes.privacy: Export only study DOI, native taxa, group animal-day/year/month-block counts, source grouped signs/means/bootstrap95. Do not expose source GPS tag IDs, original source coordinates, raw GPS, exact original dates/times, original track or per-tag coefficients.

historical_constraints.no_weather_or_solar_causality: NO ERA5 is fetched. Photoperiod is deterministic reference astronomical daylength; same calendar dates do not mean identical physical sunlight, resources, temperature, predation or habitat.
